pmc.title: Training load chart
pmc.aria: Chronic and acute load lines with load balance bars over the last {n} {n|day|days}
pmc.tip:
Chronic load, acute load and load balance over the last {n} {n|day|days} (switch to 7, 42 or 90 days next to the title; the choice is remembered).
How to read: blue = chronic load (42-day average load), orange = acute load (7 days); bars = load balance, coloured by load balance ÷ chronic load: red < −30% High Risk, green −30 to −10% Optimal, light purple −10 to +10% grey zone, purple +10 to +35% Fresh, yellow > +35% Transition (under a chronic load of 30, of 30).
Load balance = yesterday's chronic load − acute load: positive = room to spare, negative = still building fatigue.
Look for: blue rising = getting fitter; orange above blue = training more than usual lately; negative load balance is not bad.
Method: the Banister model, as applied to power training by Coggan; bands from Friel, rules of thumb, a direction only. Other platforms often call these CTL, ATL and TSB.
Training load is on the same scale as TrainingPeaks' TSS® (one hour at threshold = 100), so the numbers are roughly comparable, but details differ (e.g. moving time only, a climbing bonus), so they will not match exactly. TSS® is a registered trademark of TrainingPeaks, LLC.

split.tip:
Moving time of this period's endurance activities, split into three heart-rate bands.
How to read: low < AeT, moderate AeT–LTHR, high ≥ LTHR; bar length = share.
Look for: 75% low intensity is the floor, 80% the target (≥ 90% in base); this is a reminder, not a condition for unlocking Zone 3.
Method: Seiler 2006.

b2b.title: B2B long days
gloss.aet:
AeT, the aerobic threshold (≈ LT1, the first ventilatory threshold): the highest intensity at which you can still breathe through your nose and speak in full sentences. Every easy session of the base phase stays below it.

How to test (HR drift test):
1. A 50-min weekday slot: a treadmill at 2–3% in an air-conditioned room with a fan (best), or a flat loop early in the morning (no trails); note the temperature, heat pushes the result up; warm up 10 min until you sweat
2. Start at the HR you guess is your AeT and run 40 min at a steady power (Uphill Athlete: if you only have 40 min, do 40; not shorter), no stops, no surges; if at minute 10 of the main part HR is already 10 beats above the start and still rising → the start was too high: stop and test another day at a slower pace (Evoke); start about 5 bpm lower (estimate)
3. Compare power ÷ HR of the first and the last 20 min: drift < 3.5% → AeT can be higher; 3.5–5% → the first half's HR is your AeT; > 5% → set too high
4. The review card and the overview's Test card then offer "Apply this AeT" (untested: estimated as 0.89 × LTHR)

gloss.cp:
CP, critical power: the highest power you can hold for a long time (for running, about the intensity of a 30–60 min race).

How to test (pick one in the plan preferences):
• Quick (default, about 37 min): warm up 12 min with 3 strides → 20 min all-out, evenly paced → cool down 5 min
• Standard (about 70 min): warm up 15 min → 12 min all-out → walk / jog 30 min (don't cut it short) → 3 min all-out → cool down 10 min
• A race: a 5–10 km race or time trial
CP is computed automatically (a PD model fitted to the top edge of your last 90 days' power curve): a test is just one all-out effort on that curve, and the plan's CP is the modelled threshold power fitted to its top edge (it changes only by 3 W or more), nothing to set; test every 4–6 weeks, not within 10 days of a race
gloss.gate:
Interval gate: when the base phase may schedule intervals (pick the method in the plan preferences; each option's ? explains it).

Automatic (default): with a tested AeT (within 16 weeks) and an LTHR that isn't the default → Uphill Athlete's gap method (LTHR ÷ AeT − 1 ≤ 10%), or Friel's drift < 5%; without a tested AeT → no gate, at most once a week, decided by the guardrails: low intensity ≥ 75%, chronic load < +5 a week, weekly volume step ≤ 10%, fartlek in a 3:1 recovery week, load balance. Doses 5×1 min → 6×1 → 4×3 uphill → 5×3 → 4×4, then 3×8 / 4×8 just below threshold, alternating.

A method chosen without the data for it never locks you out for good: the guardrails decide meanwhile (custom).
